findings.summary: Previously: isInvalidKey matched any HTTP 403 containing PERMISSION_DENIED, which Google sets for nearly every 403 cause, so an unrelated 403 (billing off, API not enabled, IAM/referrer restriction) would permanently disable a valid key. FIXED: isInvalidKey now requires HTTP 400 + /API_KEY_INVALID|API key not valid/ (Google's actual invalid-key signal). A 403 now logs 'key kept' and throws AiServiceUnavailableError without touching the pool. New test gemini-call-runner.spec.ts:59-66 sends a realistic 403 PERMISSION_DENIED "Billing is disabled" body on a single-key pool and asserts the key still serves the next call. Now additionally confirmed live: a genuinely invalid key in the 11-key pool was dropped via exactly this HTTP-400 path, not a 403.

Previously: a vector-size/count mismatch threw before this.record(), losing the usage_records row for countTokens calls already billed. FIXED: record() now runs immediately after the Gemini calls settle, before the dimension check; gemini.client.spec.ts asserts the real token count is recorded even when the size check subsequently fails.

Not changed, by design, and accepted: segment ingestion is rejected (409 INVALID_STATE_TRANSITION) once a meeting leaves recording/paused/ended/queued (Phase 04 decision), so a changed-scope run never actually finds segments past the last chunked range in production; the tail branch is defensive. Covered at the unit level by chunker.spec.ts:93-99.
